title: Pines of Rome
hook: Four scenes under Rome’s umbrella pines, from children at play to an army marching in at dawn.

painting.title: Italian Landscape with Umbrella Pines
painting.pairingNote: Umbrella pines in the gardens of the Villa Borghese, with small figures at play in the grass below them, the very place and scene of the first movement, painted in Rome a century before Respighi.

facts: Respighi, born in Bologna, moved to Rome in 1913 to teach composition. He later said that two things in the city spoke to his imagination above all: its fountains, and the umbrella-shaped pines that appear on every horizon. *Fountains of Rome* (1916) made him famous; *Pines of Rome*, finished in the summer of 1924, was its sequel.

It is a [[symphonic-poem|symphonic poem]] in four scenes, played without a break. Respighi wrote a short note for each: children playing in the Villa Borghese; a chant rising from a catacomb; a moonlit night on the Janiculum hill with a nightingale; and an army of ancient Rome marching along the Appian Way at dawn.

The score asks for a huge orchestra with piano, celesta, organ and extra brass, some of them placed out of sight. In the third scene it also asks for a gramophone record of a real nightingale, one of the first uses of recorded sound in a concert work.
The premiere, at the Augusteo in Rome on 14 December 1924, was a triumph. Toscanini conducted the American premiere in New York in 1926, and it is still the most recorded of Respighi’s works.
bigPicture.inOneLine: children’s games (I), a hymn underground (II), a moonlit night (III), a march from silence to a blaze (IV).

movements.heading: The Pines of the Villa Borghese
movements.title: The Pines of the Villa Borghese
movements.summary: Respighi’s note: children play in the pine wood of the Villa Borghese, dance in rings, play at soldiers, and shriek like swallows at evening. The music is bright, high and noisy, with no low instruments at all, and it stops dead.

mainIdeas.name: The glitter
mainIdeas.description: trills in the woodwind, sweeps on harp and keyboard, bells and triangle.

mainIdeas.name: The game songs
mainIdeas.description: short, simple tunes like nursery rhymes, passed around the woodwind and trumpets.

stops.hear: A burst of high, bright sound: trilling flutes and clarinets, rushing harp and piano, bells
stops.happening: The children’s playground. Everything is in the treble

stops.hear: A short, catchy tune, repeated and passed between instruments
stops.happening: A ring-game song. Respighi’s wife Elsa later recalled singing him the songs she had sung while playing in these gardens as a child

stops.hear: Trumpets play bugle calls and a jaunty march; the woodwind chatter around them
stops.happening: The children play at soldiers

stops.hear: Louder and shriller, the tunes piled on top of each other
stops.happening: The games become wild

stops.label: Last 15 seconds
stops.hear: A harsh, clashing blast from the trumpets, and then nothing
stops.happening: The children vanish. The next scene follows at once

notice: Listen for the bass. There is almost none: no low strings, no tubas, no bassoons. That is why the sound is so light.
The movement does not end, it is cut off. Notice the shock of the silence.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Karajan recorded the *Pines* with the Berlin Philharmonic in the Philharmonie between December 1977 and February 1978, together with *Fountains of Rome*. On the Spotify album the *Fountains* come first, as tracks 1–4; the *Pines* are tracks 5–8.

movements.heading: The Pines near a Catacomb
movements.title: The Pines near a Catacomb
movements.summary: Suddenly we are in shadow, among the pines over the entrance to a catacomb, an early Christian burial place under the ground. From below rises a slow chant, solemn like a hymn. It swells to a huge climax and sinks back into the earth.

mainIdeas.name: The chant
mainIdeas.description: a slow, old church melody ([[plainchant|plainchant]]), first in the low strings and horns, later in the trombones.

mainIdeas.name: The distant trumpet
mainIdeas.description: another chant melody, a Sanctus from the Mass, played by a trumpet out of sight.

stops.hear: Very low, very soft: [[muted|muted]] strings, deep horns, a bass note from the organ that you feel more than hear
stops.happening: The scene changes to the catacomb

stops.hear: A slow, solemn tune in the horns and low strings, moving step by step
stops.happening: The chant, a Kyrie melody

stops.hear: A single trumpet, far away, plays a slow, pure melody over hushed strings
stops.happening: The [[offstage|offstage]] trumpet with the Sanctus chant

stops.hear: The chant returns in the trombones and lower brass, and the orchestra slowly gathers weight
stops.happening: The hymn rises from below

stops.hear: Full orchestra and organ, the chant at its loudest
stops.happening: The climax

stops.label: Last 80 seconds
stops.hear: The sound sinks and darkens; the chant fades into the depths
stops.happening: The hymn goes back under the ground

notice: The offstage trumpet should sound truly distant. Notice how much space it seems to open up.
Follow the chant from its first quiet appearance to the climax. It is the same slow melody, only louder and fuller.

movements.heading: The Pines of the Janiculum
movements.title: The Pines of the Janiculum
movements.summary: A [[nocturne|nocturne]]. A breath of wind stirs the pines on the Janiculum hill, lit by the full moon, and a nightingale sings. A clarinet plays as if dreaming; strings, harp and celesta make a soft, shimmering night. At the end the real nightingale, a recording, sings alone.

mainIdeas.name: The clarinet song
mainIdeas.description: a long, slow, floating melody, marked *come in sogno*, “as if in a dream”.

stops.hear: A few soft, rippling notes on the piano
stops.happening: Night falls. The piano opens the scene

stops.hear: A solo clarinet, very quiet, plays a long, wandering melody
stops.happening: The clarinet song, “as if in a dream”

stops.hear: The strings take up the melody, warm and hushed; harp and celesta glint around it
stops.happening: The moonlit pines

stops.hear: The music swells to a warm, full climax, then settles
stops.happening: The high point of the night

stops.hear: A real bird song, a nightingale, over soft, held chords and trills
stops.happening: The recorded nightingale

stops.label: Last 40 seconds
stops.hear: The bird sings almost alone as the orchestra fades
stops.happening: The scene dissolves into the next

notice: The nightingale is not an instrument imitating a bird. It is a recording of one, played through a loudspeaker. Respighi named the exact record in his score.
Listen to how quietly the clarinet begins, as if from another room.

movements.heading: The Pines of the Appian Way
movements.title: The Pines of the Appian Way
movements.summary: Misty dawn on the Appian Way, the old military road into Rome, guarded by lonely pines. Far off, the steady tread of countless feet. The poet imagines the ancient glories: trumpets blare, and a consul’s army marches towards the Capitol in the light of the rising sun. Five minutes of [[crescendo|crescendo]] from almost nothing to the whole orchestra, organ and extra brass.

mainIdeas.name: The tread
mainIdeas.description: a slow, heavy, regular beat in the timpani, piano and low strings, over a deep held organ note.

mainIdeas.name: The melody
mainIdeas.description: a long, curling tune, first on the cor anglais.

mainIdeas.name: The buccine
mainIdeas.description: ancient Roman trumpets, played by extra brass (usually flugelhorns), sometimes placed away from the orchestra.

stops.hear: Almost silence: a soft, steady thud in the timpani and low piano, a deep organ note underneath
stops.happening: The army’s tread, very far away. A [[pedal-note|pedal note]] holds the bass

stops.hear: A cor anglais plays a long, winding, sad melody above the tread
stops.happening: The melody, in the mist

stops.hear: The tread grows; horns and trumpets take up the melody; the sound thickens
stops.happening: The army comes closer

stops.hear: Extra brass break in with fanfares, answered by the orchestra
stops.happening: The buccine, the Roman trumpets

stops.hear: Everyone together, louder and louder: brass, organ, cymbals, the melody hammered out
stops.happening: The march at full strength. The climax of the whole work

stops.label: Last 30 seconds
stops.hear: A blazing major chord, held, with the full weight of the organ and the brass
stops.happening: The army reaches the Capitol

notice: Follow the steady beat from the first second to the last. It never changes speed; only its volume grows.
Listen for the moment the extra brass enter. In some performances they play from offstage or from elsewhere in the hall.

threads.title: Four pines, four times
threads.body: Each scene is set among the pines in a different place and a different time of day: morning play, a dark underground, night, and dawn. Each also goes further back in history, from children in the modern city to the early Christians to the armies of ancient Rome.

threads.title: Colour as the subject
threads.body: Respighi studied orchestration with Rimsky-Korsakov in Russia, and this music is above all about sound: no bass in the first scene, no light in the second, moonlight in the third, and everything at once in the last.

threads.title: Sound from elsewhere
threads.body: A trumpet out of sight, a recorded bird, extra brass in the gallery: Respighi places some sounds outside the orchestra to make the space feel larger.
